name: placement
kind: installation of the poll-wait booking only (rule P'), on top of version 3's installed rules S, T, D, B, M, F; frozen before any replay with it. P' changes no converted instruction and no cycle: the fold of 370bf919 stays, the converter adds one fact to the surviving poll and the engine's stall ledger books the wait there
why: placement_basic v1 Q1: the hardware books a poll wait on the first instruction that waits for the FIRST poll's result (0 on the out-of-line loop for waits below the time-out, 3876.6-3877.1 cycles per wait there at k = 1024 and the rest in the loop); the replay books it behind the last poll of the traced run. Rule P of versions 1-3 moved the surviving instruction and broke 37 full-GPU cases (version 3, last addendum). full-place3b: per-pc error inside mbarrier-poll sites 23.2 / 54.3 points.
data_seen_before_freezing: Everything in versions 1-3 and their addenda, including full-place3 (P of version 3 on the 482 / 481 cases that completed: per-pc 0.618 / 0.716) and the pdiag job dumps.

rules.P' (converter fact): Poll fold unchanged (370bf919). For a folded sequence whose first folded poll P0 has another code address than the surviving final poll: W0 = the first record behind P0 in the warp's traced stream, at most 4 records ahead, whose static control word's wait mask contains P0's write barrier (poll records included). If P0 writes a barrier and W0 exists, the surviving poll's mbarrier_wait row carries flag 0x200 (wait origin) and W0's absolute code address (the address space of the job's code-address table) in the row's otherwise unused field earliest_issue. Otherwise no flag. Nothing else of the converted stream changes.
rules.P' (ledger): While a warp is held by the pending result of a poll instance that carries the wait origin, the cycles the ledger books today under reasons beginning with barrier:SYNCS.PHASECHK for that pending result are booked, under the same reason, on the wait-origin code address for the first O cycles of that wait (counted from the first held cycle) and where they are booked today beyond O. O = origin_hold_cycles, new field of the leaf synchronization.mbarrier.trywait_timeout: 3877 on both devices (measured: placement_basic v1, the inline reader's long_scoreboard per wait at k = 1024, 3876.6 / 3876.8 h100, 3877.1 b300; source placement.<device>.v1); absent or 0: no cap is known and the booking of today stays. Statistics only: no cycle, result or journal changes; without --stall-ledger nothing changes.

criteria.K5a: u.pollcute.k0, .k64, .k256 (both devices): at least 90 % of the replay's barrier:SYNCS.PHASECHK cycles are on the readers of the inline try_waits (the BRA behind each inline TRYWAIT) and at most 1.0 cycle per wait of barrier:SYNCS.PHASECHK is on the pcs of the out-of-line loops.
criteria.K5b: u.pollcute.k1024: barrier:SYNCS.PHASECHK on the inline readers is between 3800 and 3950 cycles per wait.
criteria.K6: Every probe cell of the twelve sources has a ledger, exactly the cycles of the replay placement-v3r2 (build 3b5718c2) and the same total ledger residency (sum of all residency rows).
criteria.K7: Scoreboard (all sources): overall pc x class error not higher than placement-v3r2's on either device; no source's class error higher by more than 0.005.
criteria.K8 (full GPU, required for keeping P'): 500 / 500 cases complete on both sets and every case has the cycles of full-mio4 (cycles_equal: different 0).

decision: All of K5a, K5b, K6, K7, K8 pass on a device: P' stays on that device. A criterion fails because the implementation does not do what the rule says: corrected and repeated, stated in the addenda. Otherwise P' is taken out (the flag is not written, the leaf field removed) and the addenda say so.
hypotheses_full_gpu: Not criteria: the per-pc error inside mbarrier-poll sites (23.2 / 54.3 points in full-place3b) falls towards the 15.1 / 29.4 seen with version 3's P; site and class totals do not move (same reason, same cycles); waits whose first poll already succeeded in the traced run but which hardware entered the loop for, and the hint form's suspended sleep, stay where they are.
not_installed_here: The try_wait time-out as engine timing; the out-of-line path beyond the time-out (the cycles beyond O stay on the traced run's pcs, the hardware books them on NANOSLEEP.SYNCS); suspended:sleep intervals of the hint form.
not_allowed: No value from another machine or from the literature; no full-GPU case used to choose a rule or a value; no cell dropped after its replay is seen; criteria unchanged after freezing.

addenda.text: TWO ERRORS OF THIS PROTOCOL FOUND. (1) origin_hold_cycles = 3877 is a misreading. In u.pollcute each wait site is run by one warp of the pair; the table value 3876.6-3877.1 is the per-warp average over both warps. Per wait the hardware holds the inline reader 7754 cycles at k = 1024 (both devices; then 1470-1700 on NANOSLEEP.SYNCS), the replay 3877. K5b compared the replay's per-wait value with that halved hardware value and passed for the wrong reason. (Per call on a never-completing barrier, s.mbar_trywait_fail, the time-out is 3876; why a wait next to a running warp holds twice that is not known. u.handoff.k1024's one false result per wait of 9340 cycles fits 7754, not 3876.) (2) The reach of 4 records for the wait origin had no measurement behind it; compiled code puts the first waiter 5-16 instructions behind the poll and the hardware books the wait there (cutlass_stream_k_splitk_05: 40.7 % of the residency on a reader 6 behind). SPLIT of the per-pc error inside poll sites (points, h100 / b300), by level: the total poll-site time differs 3.56 / 4.81; the time is on another wait of the kernel (another poll group) 4.25 / 6.00; between an inline poll and its own retry loop 7.20 / 22.81; between instructions of one site 1.12 / 1.98. The first two (7.8 / 10.8) are not a matter of booking. Cap: with 7754 the total is 15.58 / 32.61, unlimited 15.52 / 31.77 (unlimited overshoots: more time on the inline reader than the hardware where the hardware did enter the loop). At 7754 the inline-against-loop part is 6.71 / 19.96; the replay in the loop where the hardware is on the inline reader 4.85 / 15.16, of which: polls folded, first waiter 5-16 behind (no origin by the reach) 2.75 / 3.27; no waiter within 16 0.12 / 0.62; the failed inline poll is still in the stream because the fold key of the loop's polls differs 0.11 / 5.66; still in the stream because an instruction the fold does not accept lies between (MUFU, LDL, P2R, LDC, ...) 0.38 / 1.93; an origin exists and the time is still in the loop 0.57 / 1.38 (not explained); loop entry not attributable 0.92 / 2.31. Other inline-against-loop parts 1.87 / 4.81. FOLD KEY: the tracer's address of a SYNCS operand of the form [R+URZ+imm] differs from that of [UR+imm] for the same barrier by a constant per capture (32649, 4, 16392, 488, 1073758272, 136316048 seen), and the fold keys polls by that address; checked on traces: 6 of 13 b300 cases looked at have it (2747-8107 inline polls each), 0 of 6 h100 cases. CHECKS: the poll groups are built from the replayed transitions and static branches; P' moves time only inside a group, and the between-groups level differs between full-place3b and full-place4 by 0.23 / 0.59 points (the grouping's error). The classes agree with the trace of the dominant site in 13 of 13 cases compared (first-waiter distance 6 / 8 / 8 / 9 / none; key mismatch; rejected instruction). An earlier static attempt (operand form alone) mislabelled reach and cap cases as key mismatch and was dropped. Reachable by booking rules if all four were right: about 3.8 / 13.8 points (cap 0.6 / 3.0, reach 2.75 / 3.27, key 0.11 / 5.66, rejected instruction 0.38 / 1.93); not promised, and the counterfactual replays are diagnostics, not a way to choose the leaf.
